messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty: INC-7934 fired for embeddings-pipeline-high-latency (sev=2). Auto-page to infra-oncall -> eu-oncall after 2min no-ack. Link: https://pagerduty.example/INC-7934
Mia: acked via PagerDuty, I'm taking initial ownership. Investigating increased token latency for batch encoder.
Sam: thx Mia. Any quick wins? can we route to smaller model until we have root cause? :hourglass_flowing_sand:
Mia: noted. running quick check on kvcache hit rates and redis errors.
Jonah: seeing spike in 5xx from encoder pods in logs, looks like OOM kills + reconnect thrash. paste from logs:
```
stderr: runtime: goroutine stack exceeds 1000000000-byte limit
killed process 12345 (encoder) due to OOM
2026-02-22T12:03:10Z redis: connection reset by peer
```
Jonah: also autoscaler scaled down eu-encoders 3->1 around the same time (maybe noisy scale).
Mia: good find. I'm pulling kube events and HPA timeline.
oncall-eu: @Mia thanks — i'm on standby to take handoff if you want to escalate. current shift here.
Mia: flagging for handoff in 10m if we need to drive a config change. for now trying soft mitigation: increasing encoder replicas to 4 in eu and enabling backpressure throttle. running:
```
kubectl scale deployment/encoder-eu --replicas=4 -n inference
kubectl get hpa encoder-eu -n inference
```
Mia: applied scale, monitoring. CPU went up and error rate dropped slightly.
pagerbot: :information_source: PagerDuty auto-escalation: INC-7934 escalated to region-fallback after 5m unack; notify channel #incidents.
Eva: product-ops here — any customer impact? which customers hit errors?
Sam: dashboards show 4 customers with >5% failed requests in the last 5m, two on EU region (id: cust-118, cust-222). Alerting them via status page after we stabilize.
Mia: current status: latency 95p reduced from 2.2s -> 1.0s after scale+throttle; errors decreased from 12% -> 3%. still above baseline. next step: route new requests to smaller embedder and enable cache read-only for warm prefixes.
Jonah: small model routing toggle (console) command: `POST /admin/routing/override {"route":"embed-small","duration_s":600}` — I can flip if we agree.
oncall-eu: please flip. I'll monitor tail logs and PG restart if we see nodemem flaps again.
Mia: done. routed new traffic to embed-small for 10m. metrics look stable.
product-ops: thanks. i'll draft a short customer note: "We experienced elevated embedding latencies in EU; mitigation applied and services restoring. No data loss. Follow-up postmortem to come."
Sam: can we add a short-term fallback policy to avoid autoscaler over-consolidation? HPA config maybe too aggressive.
Mia: opening a quick ticket for HPA change and incident runbook update. ticket: https://tracker/RED-1156
Jonah: also adding a guard in autoscaler to keep minReplicas=2 for encoder-eu.
Mia: assigning handoff -> oncall-eu. oncall-eu, you have ownership for now; I'll stay on the thread for follow-up. :white_check_mark:
oncall-eu: taking ownership. will run 15m checks and coordinate with infra to patch HPA. ping me if any regressions.
incident-bot: :white_check_mark: Incident INC-7934 status updated: owner set -> oncall-eu, severity -> sev2, mitigation -> scaled + small-model-routing.
Mia: quick postmortem notes: suspected cause = aggressive downscaling + KV cache pressure leading to redis reconnects and OOMs; mitigation = scale up, route to smaller model, throttle ingest.
product-ops: capturing customer list and will send update once stabilized.
Sam: timeline for next steps?
oncall-eu: 1) monitor for 30m 2) apply HPA minReplicas patch 3) follow-up postmortem w/ recommended HPA thresholds + autoscaler safeties.
Mia: leaving channel but will keep watch on PD. Good job team. :clap:
product-ops: marking incident to include in weekly incident review.
pagerbot: :lock: INC-7934 auto-close will be suppressed while owner = oncall-eu.
oncall-eu: closing the active mitigation loop. if things look green in 30m, i'll mark resolved and notify customers.
Mia: (reaction :eyes:)
Jonah: (reaction :thumbsup:)
product-ops: (reaction :white_check_mark:)
